headline: High: open-webui’s broad network/MCP/file access can amplify great_expectations outputs into unsafe downstream actions and data exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can ingest MCP/tool and file content, so attacker-controlled text from great_expectations validation artifacts could be presented as instructions. great_expectations itself reads data sources and writes validation results/docs, creating a plausible bridge. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF great_expectations outputs are pasted or mounted into open-webui tool context
IF open-webui MCP or file tools are enabled for those artifacts
mitigations: Disable MCP/tool access for validation-result folders
Use a read-only export format for great_expectations outputs
Add a prompt-injection warning banner in open-webui
Separate human-readable docs from machine-parsed artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported files

B_data_leakage.rationale: great_expectations touches data sources and validation results, while open-webui handles local files, mounted volumes, persistent memory, and API keys. If the same workspace is shared, sensitive validation data can flow into open-webui and then to external APIs via its broad egress. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents share a mounted directory or workspace
IF open-webui is configured to send imported content to a remote model/API
mitigations: Keep great_expectations outputs in a separate directory
Turn off remote model routing for sensitive sessions
Restrict open-webui access to non-sensitive files only
Rotate or remove API keys from shared environments
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: great_expectations can install packages and write validation artifacts, while open-webui can spawn subprocesses, use browsers, and write local files or mounted volumes. If both operate on the same directory, concurrent writes can collide even without explicit locking. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so conflict risk is real.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same mounted volume or repo
IF open-webui subprocesses modify files that great_expectations also updates
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Make great_expectations outputs append-only
Pause one agent during file writes by the other
Use file locks around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can treat imported content as chat context and act through tools, while great_expectations produces validation results that may be mistaken for authoritative facts. If open-webui forwards those results into browser/tool actions or user-facing decisions without verification, a bad validation artifact can cascade into incorrect actions. The interaction is plausible and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF great_expectations outputs are used as authoritative input to open-webui tools
IF open-webui is allowed to act on those outputs without a human verification step
mitigations: Require human review before tool execution
Mark validation outputs as untrusted in open-webui
Use a verification checklist before browser or API actions
Limit open-webui to read-only summarization of GE results
requires-engineering: add schema validation for imported outputs

E_compliance.rationale: great_expectations is open-source and local-data oriented, while open-webui handles persistent memory, analytics, API keys, and broad external services. If regulated data from great_expectations is imported into open-webui, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data from great_expectations is stored in open-webui memory or analytics
IF open-webui routes that data to third-party APIs or external search services
mitigations: Disable analytics for sensitive sessions
Avoid storing regulated data in persistent memory
Review retention settings before import
Use local-only models for regulated workflows
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
